items.title: How Conversational AI Is Moving Hotel Linen Management From Reactive to Proactive
items.snippet: A conversational AI assistant built on RFID inventory data lets hotel operators query linen stock, loss trends, and reorder needs in plain language, shifting from reactive to predictive management.

items.title: First Look: Inside JetBlue’s New BlueFirst
items.snippet: JetBlue unveils BlueFirst, its new domestic first-class cabin, featuring plush recliners, upgraded entertainment, creative dining and competitive fares, as the airline prepares its December debut and premium expansion across America.

items.title: MCR’s Tyler Morse Wants to Ban AI Bots From Booking His Hotels
items.snippet: " He prefers human customers, who can more easily be persuaded to make impulse purchases. Tyler Morse wants to stop personal AI agents from booking rooms at his hotels. The reason isn't privacy or regulation, according to the chairman and CEO of MCR Hotels. It's that the software can't be talked into a splurge.

items.title: Hyatt Hyderabad Gachibowli Appoints Nisha Mundliya as Director of Finance and Suresh Raju as Human Resources Manager
items.snippet: Hyatt Hyderabad Gachibowli is pleased to announce the appointment of Nisha Mundliya as Director of Finance and Suresh Raju as Human Resources Manager , further strengthening the hotel’s leadership team and commitment to operational excellence and people-centric growth.

items.title: Braemar officially splits from Ashford, transitions to self-managed REIT
items.snippet: On Tuesday, the real estate investment trust terminated its advisory agreement with Ashford. It also appointed a new executive team and board of directors. On Tuesday, Braemar Hotels & Resorts entered into a termination and release agreement with Ashford Inc. and its affiliates, marking its official separation from the company and transition to a self-managed real estate investment trust, according to a Nov.

items.title: Nearly 91% of Mumbai Airport's international traffic to remain unaffected by T1 redevelopment
items.snippet: The new Terminal 1 is expected to increase the terminal's passenger-handling capacity from 15 million passengers per annum (MPPA) to 20 MPPA, a rise of about 33 per cent.

items.title: Royal Orchid eyes 35 hotels signings a year
items.snippet: With more than 125 operating hotels and over 50 projects in the pipeline, Royal Orchid Hotels is accelerating its asset-light expansion across emerging markets. The group is strengthening its Regenta portfolio, entering six states with Hampton by Hilton and targeting growing demand from domestic and pilgrimage travel.

items.title: South Africa Expands Digital Travel Authorisation for Indians
items.snippet: South Africa has expanded its Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) system, introducing new features to simplify travel planning for eligible visitors from India, Southeast Asia and the Middle East. The enhanced digital platform aims to make travel authorisation more accessible and convenient, encouraging international visitors to explore the country’s wildlife, landscapes, cities and cultural heritage.

items.title: Vietjet Celebrates Diwali Onboard Bengaluru Ho Chi Minh Flights
items.snippet: Vietjet celebrated India’s Festival of Lights by bringing Diwali festivities onboard its flights between Bengaluru and Ho Chi Minh City, creating a festive experience for passengers travelling between the two destinations. The special initiative brought Indian traditions and festive cheer to the skies, allowing travellers to experience the spirit of Diwali during their journey.

items.title: Minor Hotels to enter Uzbekistan with 151-room NH Hotel Tashkent in 2027
items.snippet: Minor Hotels has signed a franchise agreement with EASYRENT PE for the 151-room NH Hotel Tashkent, marking the hospitality group’s entry into Uzbekistan and its debut in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and Central Asia. The property, currently undergoing refurbishment and repositioning under the NH Hotels & Resorts brand, is scheduled to open in the first quarter of 2027.
